sections.h2: Who handles deed recording for Sherburne County property?
sections.html:
The Recorder's Office in Elk River keeps the land records for every parcel in the county. Deeds, mortgages and related filings all land there, and staff check each one for the required information before it goes on record.

Walk-in recording needs no appointment, according to the county, although other services do. The office sits in the Government Center at 13880 Business Center Drive NW, Suite 100, Elk River, MN 55330-4668. Call 763-765-4420 with questions. Birth and death certificates come from the same counter, which can mean a line on busy days.

sections.h2: What happens after I hand over a Sherburne County deed?
sections.html:
Most sellers never touch the filing. The county recommends eRecording for anyone who submits regularly and points to the Minnesota Land Title Association directory for firms that can send documents electronically. If you bring a paper deed yourself, expect these steps:

  1. Staff read it for completeness against state requirements
  2. They confirm that the right fees came with it
  3. It gets a sequential number and a date and time stamp
  4. Clerks index it by legal description and by grantor and grantee, plus more than 20 other fields
  5. Indexing is checked, then the page is scanned and the image reviewed
  6. A receipt is prepared and the copy goes back to the presenter

The county separates two terms. Recording means a reproduction goes back to you, and filing means the office retains the original. Staff will not draft a deed or advise you on one, and the county cites Minnesota Statutes 481.02 for that rule. A real estate attorney is the right contact for drafting questions.

sections.h2: Why do Sherburne County deeds get rejected?
sections.html:
The recorder publishes the usual reasons a real estate document is sent back unrecorded. Walk through them before the closing date.

  • Back taxes remain unpaid on the parcel
  • No draftsman statement
  • Deed tax or mortgage registration tax computed wrongly
  • A legal description that does not match the records, or looks doubtful
  • A Certificate of Real Estate Value that is absent or half finished
  • No mailing name and address for future tax statements
  • A notary block with gaps
  • A recording fee that is short or over
  • Well information left off a transfer document

Most of these come down to paperwork that a title company checks routinely, which is a good reason to send the deed through one.

sections.h2: How much does the Sherburne County Recorder charge?
sections.html:
County fees follow the ceilings in Minnesota Statutes 357.18, and the recorder posts the working numbers on its title system pages.

Selected Sherburne County Recorder fees from the county's Abstract and Torrens title pages
ItemFee
Recording a deed or other document (Abstract)$46
Well certificate$54
Certified copy$10 flat
Plain copy supplied with the original$2
Satisfactions or assignments, up to 4 citations$46, plus $10 per extra citation
Plat$56
Returned check$30
Transfer of a Torrens certificate$46

The county collects no conservation fee. Deed tax, mortgage registration tax and the value certificate are handled one floor of paperwork away, at the Auditor/Treasurer's Office, so ask there for the amounts. A separate sheet of copy and use fees took effect January 1, 2026, and charges $2.00 for page one of a mailed copy and $0.50 for each page after it.

sections.h2: Abstract or Torrens: which system covers my parcel?
sections.html:
Minnesota runs two land systems side by side, and both are recorded in this office. An abstract is a condensed history of every deed, mortgage and other document touching the land. A lender or buyer hires an attorney or title insurer to read that history and confirm the title is clear. Many Sherburne County abstracts begin with the recorded homestead documents.

Torrens works differently. A court orders a certificate of title, and that certificate is the title. The Recorder serves as Registrar of Titles under the District Court's control, with a court-appointed Examiner as adviser. Chapter 508 of Minnesota Statutes bars the Registrar from accepting certain instruments without the Examiner's certification or a court order. Call 763-765-4420 before a deed is drafted if you cannot tell which system applies, since Torrens transfers carry their own fees.

sections.h2: What well information must go on a transfer document?
sections.html:
A deed that needs a Certificate of Real Estate Value also needs well information. For a property with no wells, the document says so in a short statement, for example that the seller knows of no wells on the land.

A property with a well takes a completed Well Disclosure Certificate. A seller can skip a new certificate by stating that the number and status of wells match the last one filed. To find out whether one already exists, call the Minnesota Department of Health at 800-383-9808 or search its online well database.

Census estimates put the county at 104,194 people in mid-2025, a 7.2% rise on the April 2020 base. In 1960 it had 12,861 residents, and by 2000 it had 64,417. Elk River serves as county seat and largest city.

  • 38,457 housing units and 35,555 households of about 2.78 people
  • 83.2% of homes lived in by their owners
  • A typical owner-occupied home valued at $361,400, with typical gross rent at $1,127
  • Household income around $105,466 at the median
  • A 30.7-minute average trip to work
  • 319 permits for new buildings in 2025

The county spans 451 square miles, 433 of them land. The Mississippi bounds the south, the Rum River crosses the upper east, and the Elk River drains the west and south. Glaciers left sandy, gravelly soil that farms less easily than much of Minnesota.

sections.h2: How was Sherburne County formed, and why do old deeds mention Humboldt?
sections.html:
Lawmakers split the south end of Benton County to create Sherburne on February 25, 1856, and named it for Moses Sherburne, a territorial judge. Humboldt, now Big Lake, started as the seat. Elk River grew from two villages, Orono, platted in 1855, and Elk River Village, platted in 1865, and they merged in 1881. A county vote in 1867 moved the seat to Elk River, and Humboldt became Big Lake that year.

The boundaries have stayed as drawn in 1856. Every deed recorded since then therefore sits in one county's records, even where the village name on an old page has changed.

sections.h2: Which other recorder services help during a sale?
sections.html:
Property Watch is a free alert that contacts you by email or phone when a document is recorded under your name. The county also runs fee escrow accounts, with a $200 minimum balance, so a payment shortfall does not stall a recording.

  • State tax liens are indexed by taxpayer name, with a $30 fee at release, and federal liens and releases cost $46
  • Completed foreclosure sales, court records and plat searches have links on the recorder's page
  • The Sheriff holds foreclosure sales at the Government Center on Tuesdays and Wednesdays at 10 a.m.
  • A Sheriff's certificate of redemption costs $250 and requires a request 10 days or more ahead

Tax statements are mailed in March with a March 31 statutory deadline. A parcel's taxes turn delinquent after the payable year ends. Ask the Auditor/Treasurer at 763-765-4350 for the amount owed before you close.

sections.h2: What state rules sit behind a Sherburne County closing?
sections.html:
For any sale above $3,000, someone must file a certificate of value with the county auditor when the deed is recorded, as Minnesota Statutes 272.115 directs. The state deed tax is .0033 of net consideration, set by section 287.21.

After a sale, the assessor drops the homestead label for the next assessment year unless the new owner applies and qualifies.

faqs.q: What is the street address of the Sherburne County Recorder?
faqs.a: 13880 Business Center Drive NW, Suite 100, Elk River, MN 55330-4668. Staff answer at 763-765-4420.

faqs.q: What is the fee for filing a deed with the Sherburne County Recorder?
faqs.a: The recording fee for an Abstract document is $46, and a well certificate adds $54 where one is required. The county does not collect a conservation fee.

faqs.q: Do I need an appointment to record a document?
faqs.a: No. The county states that no appointment is needed to record a document, though some other services require one.

faqs.q: Where do I pay deed tax in Sherburne County?
faqs.a: Contact the Auditor/Treasurer's Office, which handles deed tax, mortgage registration tax and the Certificate of Real Estate Value. The number for property tax questions is 763-765-4350.

faqs.q: Can I check who recorded a document against my name?
faqs.a: Yes. The Property Watch service is a free subscription that notifies you by email or phone when a document is recorded under your name.
